title: Directed monomorphic sheaf cocones are colimits under joint stalk coverage
statement: Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preordered set in the universe of a topological space $X$. Let $D:I\to\operatorname{Ab}(X)$ and let $c:D\to F$ be a cocone of abelian sheaves [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. Suppose every $c_i$ is monic and for every $x\in X$ and $t\in F_x$ there are $i$ and $s\in(D_i)_x$ with $(c_i)_x(s)=t$, using stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Then $(F,c)$ is a colimit cocone [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. No compactness or basis hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 02UX (lemma-vanishing-generated-one-section), first paragraph of the proof

proof.text: Map the cocone to underlying sets of each stalk. Joint stalk coverage gives the surjectivity condition in Mathlib Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf'. A stalk map of a monic sheaf map is monic by Presheaf.mono_iff_stalk_mono, hence injective by AddCommGrpCat.mono_iff_injective. Thus equal elements at a single stage are already equal there, giving the injectivity condition with its identity arrow. The Mathlib criterion proves the mapped cocone is a colimit.

Take the existing sheaf colimit and its comparison m to the given cocone. Stalks followed by the abelian-group forgetful functor preserve the filtered colimit. Both mapped cocones are colimits, so IsColimit.hom_isIso shows the mapped comparison is an isomorphism. Forgetting abelian groups reflects isomorphisms, so the comparison is an isomorphism on each stalk.
Apply Mathlib Presheaf.isIso_iff_stalkFunctor_map_iso to show m is an isomorphism of sheaves. IsColimit.ofPointIso transports the known sheaf colimit to the requested cocone.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 02UX, first paragraph; explicit implementation of its stalkwise colimit argument

mathlib_searches.query: directed colimit of subsheaves jointly surjective on stalks
A sheaf is the filtered colimit of subobjects whose stalks exhaust every stalk
mathlib_searches.results: Generic germ existence, basis germ existence, and existence of filtered sheaf colimits; no finite-generation exhaustion or directed stalk-cover criterion.

Stalk and skyscraper APIs; local Mathlib search finds Types.FilteredColimit.isColimitOf' and the stalkwise isomorphism criterion. No existing construction of finite-generator abelian subsheaf diagrams.
